title: Lena and the Ember
premise: Coral Crane has spent his life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, stealing memories from travelers to sell to those who want to forget. When the old gods resume answering prayers, the valley's protective silence begins to crack, and Coral learns he is the last living vessel of an ember — a fragment of divine fire that the vanished country of Vael hid inside a human bloodline: his own. Lena, a priestess of the reawakened gods and the one person whose memories he could never steal, comes to claim him for her faith; loving her means defying both his duty to stay hidden and hers to deliver him. Together they must find the Door of Ash, the only exit from a country that was erased from maps and memory alike, before the gods' hunger consumes the valley. In the end Coral gives up the ember — and with it every memory of Lena — to seal the door, while she chooses exile over heaven so that someone will remember him.
about_author: Juniper Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. She writes fantasy about what people choose to keep when keeping it costs everything.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He works the market at dusk, lifting memories from pilgrims who cross into the Hollow to escape their pasts. We learn the valley's rule: magic cannot follow you in, but neither can magic leave. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A traveler's stolen memory shows Coral something impossible — a god answering a prayer beyond the ridge. Lena arrives in the Hollow hunting the 'ember-bearer,' and Coral discovers he cannot steal her memories at all. Emotional beat: first crack in Coral's invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Ember Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Touching a relic Lena carries, Coral's own buried memories surface: his mother's dying words, the brand on his wrist, the truth that he is Vael's hiding place. Emotional beat: terror of inheriting a purpose he never chose.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The gods' return is fraying the valley — travelers' stolen memories bleed back, and the Hollow's elders vote to give Coral to the church rather than lose their sanctuary. Emotional beat: Lena torn between doctrine and the man she was sent to capture.

chapters.title: Running Toward the Map
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Coral flees with Lena as reluctant guide; they seek the Cartographer of Ash, last keeper of Vael's geography. Betrayal by Coral's fence, Sable, forces them off the road. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership hardening into trust.

chapters.title: The Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The Cartographer reveals the Door of Ash opens only where Vael stood — a place unmade so thoroughly that walking there means walking through forgetting itself. Each step erases one of Coral's memories. Emotional beat: love measured against self-erasure.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Sable catches them, offering to sell Coral's location to the gods' new church unless Lena surrenders her priestess vows. Lena breaks her oaths publicly to save him, becoming exiled from everything she served. Emotional beat: duty inverted — love becomes her religion.

chapters.title: Where the Gods Wait
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At Vael's border the old gods manifest, offering Coral a bargain: surrender the ember willingly and be made divine, or be taken and the valley burned. He sees what divinity costs — the Cartographer is revealed as a god who once chose mortality. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Door of Ash
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. Coral and Lena fight through the gods' servants to the Door; opening it requires the ember freely given. Coral chooses to pour himself out — every stolen memory returned, every memory of Lena surrendered — sealing the gods outside the world. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the truest form of theft reversed.

chapters.title: Someone Will Remember
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Resolution. The valley stands, ordinary and safe; Coral lives, hollowed, not knowing her. Lena, exiled from heaven by choice, stays beside him and begins telling him their story from the beginning — the one inheritance the gods cannot take. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into devotion.
